name: Install prompt (beforeinstallprompt) and manifest install
plain: Lets a site offer to install itself as an app on the device.
meaning: An installed app gets its own window and icon, and unlocks install only features (badging, file handling, shortcuts).

web.api: window.addEventListener('beforeinstallprompt', e=>e.prompt()); manifest.webmanifest with name, icons, start_url, display, id

access.prompt_ui: Browser install dialog; Add to Home Screen sheet on iOS
access.iframe: Same as top level; cross-origin iframes need a permissions policy where listed

chrome.note: display and/or display_override are required for a web app to be installable.

edge.note: display and/or display_override are required for a web app to be installable.

safari.note: Add to Dock on macOS; no beforeinstallprompt

ios_safari.note: Add to Home Screen via Share sheet

chrome_android.note: display and/or display_override are required for a web app to be installable.

samsung.note: display and/or display_override are required for a web app to be installable.

data.metric: Lets a site offer to install itself as an app on the device.

limits.headline: Can offer to install the site as an app, but only you can accept
limits.user_action: You tap Install app, or Add to Home Screen on iPhone
can: Show an install offer after you tap a button on the page
Give the site its own window and icon once you accept
Unlock install only features like badges, file opening and shortcuts
cannot: Install anything without your say so
Skip the browser's own install dialog
Show an install button on Safari, where you add the site from the Share menu
Install in Firefox on computers, which has no install
limits.reach_label: One install, if you say yes
limits.differs: Chrome, Edge and Samsung Internet offer a prompt. On iPhone you add the site from the Share menu. Firefox on computers has no install.

story.what_it_is: A site can offer to install itself as an app on your device, with its own icon and window.

marketing.name: Making PWAs installable
marketing.pitch: Sites that meet some rules can be installed from the browser like an app, without an app store.

marketing.name: Add to Dock in Safari
marketing.pitch: Safari 17 lets any website be added to the Mac Dock as a web app.

story.for_you: You may see an Install button or banner. After you tap it, the site gets its own icon and window and feels like an app. You can remove it any time.
story.for_makers: Makers skip app stores and fees, ship one codebase and get an icon on the home screen. Installed apps get more features like push and badging. Install rates are a growth metric for them.

use_cases.example: Instagram or X offers an Install button, and the site becomes an icon with a full screen window.
A browser game offers to install, so it opens full screen and loads offline from the home screen.
A web music player installs as its own app with media keys.
A store installs as an app and sends push alerts for deals.
A web design or office tool installs to feel like a desktop program.
A web cloud gaming service installs so it runs full screen with controller support.
A travel site installs for offline boarding passes and trip details.
A news site installs as an app, to get push alerts and an icon.

technical_bounds: iOS needs manual Share > Add to Home Screen
In the EU, non WebKit engines may not support install on iOS

history.change: Safari 17 adds Add to Dock on macOS
Every Home Screen site opens as a web app by default
Chrome on iOS gets Add to Home Screen after iOS 16.4
